title: RecyclerView internals
scopeHtml: Recycling model, ViewHolder rules, caches, DiffUtil, payloads, stable ids, item animators, prefetch, nested lists, LayoutManagers, ConcatAdapter, click handling and production bugs. Numbers marked "verify" were not confirmed against source in this session (docs search was partial); check against your RecyclerView version (1.2.x / 1.3.x).

questions.promptHtml: How does RecyclerView avoid creating a view for every item in a 10,000-item list? Walk me through what happens when the user scrolls one row.

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Checks whether you know it is a view-reuse system with a data-binding step, not a "smart ListView".

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: I keep only enough ViewHolders to fill the screen plus a few spares. When a row scrolls off, its holder goes to a cache or pool. When a new row appears, RecyclerView takes a holder from there and calls onBindViewHolder to rewrite its contents, instead of inflating. Inflation (onCreateViewHolder) only happens when nothing reusable exists.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
Three roles: the Adapter (data to holders), the LayoutManager (decides position of each child and asks for holders), and the Recycler (stores and hands out detached holders). On scroll, LayoutManager calls fill(): it recycles children that left the viewport (removeAndRecycleView) and asks recycler.getViewForPosition(pos) for new ones at the leading edge.

scroll up by 1 row
 top row leaves viewport  -> Recycler.recycleView -> mCachedViews (size 2) -> overflow -> RecycledViewPool (5 per type)
 new row at bottom        -> getViewForPosition -> cache hit (position match, NO rebind)
                                                -> pool hit (rebind via onBindViewHolder)
                                                -> miss (onCreateViewHolder + onBind)

A holder from the pool needs a bind because it carries another item's data. A holder from the view cache for the exact same position is reused as is (no bind) as long as it is not invalidated.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
class UserAdapter : RecyclerView.Adapter<UserAdapter.VH>() {
    var items: List<User> = emptyList()
    class VH(val b: ItemUserBinding) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(b.root)
    override fun onCreateViewHolder(p: ViewGroup, t: Int) =
        VH(ItemUserBinding.inflate(LayoutInflater.from(p.context), p, false)) // once per holder
    override fun onBindViewHolder(h: VH, pos: Int) { h.b.name.text = items[pos].name } // every reuse
    override fun getItemCount() = items.size
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Saying "RecyclerView recycles the data". It recycles views; data must be rebound every time.
  • Inflating in onBindViewHolder.
  • Believing the number of holders equals the list size; typically ~visible + 2 cache + prefetch.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Why inflate(..., parent, false)? -> Parent is needed to resolve LayoutParams; attaching would add the child twice and crash.
  2. Why is it faster than ListView? -> Mandatory ViewHolder, layout-manager separation, item animations, DiffUtil, finer-grained caches.
  3. When is onCreateViewHolder called a lot? -> Different view types, small pool, nested lists, or notifyDataSetChanged plus invalid holders in some cases.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: "ViewHolder pattern reuses views". Senior: names the Recycler tiers, says which reuse needs a rebind, and ties it to pool sizing and prefetch.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Teams inflating inside bind saw 25 ms+ frames on first fling; moving inflation to create fixed it.

questions.promptHtml: What are the rules for onBindViewHolder? What must never go there and what happens to view state after a holder is reused?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: The most common source of RecyclerView bugs is violating the "bind must fully overwrite state" rule.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: Bind runs every time a holder is assigned a new position, so it must set every visible property from the data, including the "empty" and "off" cases. No inflation, no network, no heavy work, no capturing position in long-lived listeners. Any state not written by bind leaks from the previous item.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
Holder states: created (onCreateViewHolder) -> bound -> attached to window (onViewAttachedToWindow) -> detached (onViewDetachedFromWindow) -> recycled (onViewRecycled, release resources here) -> pool -> rebound at another position. onViewRecycled is your hook to cancel image loads, stop animations, and clear listeners. onFailedToRecycleView fires for views with transient state (e.g. running animation); return true to force recycling.

Rules:

  1. Bind is idempotent and complete: every branch sets every field (if (done) strike() else clearStrike()).
  2. Fast: p95 under a few ms; frame budget is 16.6 ms at 60 Hz, 8.3 ms at 120 Hz, and bind is only part of it (also measure/layout/draw).
  3. Don't hold position int in a lambda; use bindingAdapterPosition at click time.
  4. Transient UI state (checked, expanded) lives in the data model, not in the view.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
override fun onBindViewHolder(h: VH, pos: Int) {
    val t = items[pos]
    h.b.title.text = t.title
    h.b.check.isChecked = t.done          // always set, true or false
    h.b.title.paintFlags = if (t.done) h.b.title.paintFlags or Paint.STRIKE_THRU_TEXT_FLAG
        else h.b.title.paintFlags and Paint.STRIKE_THRU_TEXT_FLAG.inv()
}
override fun onViewRecycled(h: VH) { Glide.with(h.b.img).clear(h.b.img) }

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Only setting the "true" branch, so reused rows show stale checkmarks.
  • Setting OnCheckedChangeListener before isChecked, firing spurious callbacks; set value first or null the listener.
  • Starting async work in bind with no cancel in recycle: image for row 3 lands on row 40.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. onViewRecycled vs onViewDetachedFromWindow? -> Detached can happen while the holder is kept (scrap/cache); recycled means it is going to the pool.
  2. Where do you start/stop animations? -> Attached/detached for lifecycle-bound ones.
  3. Why can onBindViewHolder be called for a position twice without scrolling? -> Invalidation, notifyItemChanged, layout passes with scrap that was invalidated.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE lists "don't inflate". Senior adds recycle hooks, async-cancel discipline, state in the model, and the click-position rule.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A "mark as read" list showed wrong rows highlighted after fast scroll because only the highlight branch was set.

questions.promptHtml: Explain RecyclerView's cache levels and the order in which getViewForPosition looks for a holder. Which tiers avoid a rebind?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Separates people who memorised "ViewHolder pattern" from those who can reason about why a scroll rebinds or recreates.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: Lookup order: attached scrap and changed scrap (holders pulled off during the current layout pass), then the view cache (default 2, matched by position, no rebind), then the optional ViewCacheExtension (rarely used), then the RecycledViewPool (default 5 per view type, needs rebind), and finally onCreateViewHolder. Only scrap/cache hits by position skip bind.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html:
getViewForPosition(pos)
 1 mChangedScrap (only when pre-layout / animations)   -> by position / id
 2 mAttachedScrap (by position, then by stable id)     -> no rebind if valid
 3 hidden views (being animated out)
 4 mCachedViews   (ArrayList, size 2 default)          -> match POSITION, no rebind if valid
 5 ViewCacheExtension (user supplied, rarely)
 6 RecycledViewPool (SparseArray viewType -> ArrayList, 5 each) -> bind needed
 7 adapter.createViewHolder -> onCreateViewHolder + onBind

Scrap is temporary: during onLayoutChildren the LayoutManager calls detachAndScrapAttachedViews, then re-attaches by position, so a relayout with no data change rebinds nothing. After the pass, leftovers are recycled. When the cache (2) overflows, the oldest goes to the pool; when the pool slot for that type is full (5), the holder is discarded and GC'd. Invalid holders (after notifyDataSetChanged without stable ids) skip scrap/cache and go to the pool, which is why a full refresh rebinds everything. Defaults (2 and 5) are from AndroidX source constants DEFAULT_CACHE_SIZE and DEFAULT_MAX_SCRAP; verify for your version.

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Thinking the pool keys by position; it keys by viewType only.
  • Thinking cached views are rebinding-free for any position; they match the same position.
  • Assuming ViewCacheExtension is a general cache (docs: Recycler never sends views to it).

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Why does scrolling back one row not rebind? -> View cache hit by position.
  2. How would you reduce rebinds on a back-and-forth scrolling list? -> Raise setItemViewCacheSize, memory cost per holder.
  3. What happens with a pool shared by two RecyclerViews with different holder classes for the same viewType int? -> ClassCastException on reuse; viewTypes must map to the same layout/holder.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: 3-YOE: "there is a cache and a pool". Senior: gives order, keys (position vs viewType), which tiers rebind, scrap's relation to layout, and sizing consequences.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Chat list with 8 view types and pool size 5 inflated during every fling; setMaxRecycledViews per type fixed it.

questions.promptHtml: How do DiffUtil, ListAdapter and AsyncListDiffer fit together, and what do areItemsTheSame and areContentsTheSame mean?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Basic modern list plumbing; wrong equality implementations are a top bug.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: DiffUtil computes the minimal set of insert/remove/move/change operations between two lists. areItemsTheSame asks "same logical entity?" (compare ids). areContentsTheSame asks "same visible data?" (usually ==). AsyncListDiffer runs the diff on a background thread and dispatches results on main; ListAdapter is an adapter wrapping an AsyncListDiffer so you call submitList.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Algorithm is Myers' diff; cost O(N + D^2) worst case where D is edit distance, plus optional move detection (detectMoves, extra cost). Because it is O(N+D^2), very large lists with massive changes (100k items fully reordered) can take noticeable time even in background. ListAdapter's submitList(new): if new === current it is ignored (no diff); a newer submit supersedes an in-flight diff via a generation counter, so only the latest result is dispatched. submitList(list, commitCallback) runs the callback after the list is committed (use it to scroll to top after insert).

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
object Diff : DiffUtil.ItemCallback<User>() {
    override fun areItemsTheSame(a: User, b: User) = a.id == b.id
    override fun areContentsTheSame(a: User, b: User) = a == b   // data class
}
class UserAdapter : ListAdapter<User, VH>(Diff) { /* getItem(pos) */ }
adapter.submitList(newList) { recycler.scrollToPosition(0) }

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• areItemsTheSame comparing whole objects, so every edit looks like remove+insert (flicker, lost animations).
  • Mutating the list you already submitted then resubmitting it: same instance, ignored.
  • Content class with var fields mutated in place: old and new are the same object, diff sees equal.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Why immutable models? -> Old/new snapshots must be distinct and stable while the diff runs on a background thread.
  2. What if areContentsTheSame returns false for every item? -> Every row rebinds on each submit.
  3. What is the cost on 50k items? -> Roughly linear when few edits, quadratic in edit distance; measure and consider paging.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior adds threading and generation semantics, same-instance pitfall, move-detection cost, and commitCallback.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Feed whose posts mutated like-counts in place never updated; fixed by copying data classes.

questions.promptHtml: Why is notifyDataSetChanged() considered a last resort, and what do you use instead?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Quick check of whether you know it kills animations, scroll position stability and caching.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: notifyDataSetChanged tells RecyclerView "everything may have changed". It invalidates all holders, so every visible row is rebound, caches are bypassed, and the item animator cannot animate (flash). Use notifyItemInserted/Removed/Changed/Moved/RangeX, or better DiffUtil via ListAdapter, so only the actual changes are touched.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: With setHasStableIds(true) the data-set-changed path can map holders by id and avoid some work, but it is still a full-invalidate. Granular calls must be correct: wrong indices cause IndexOutOfBoundsException: Inconsistency detected. Invalid view holder adapter positionViewHolder, a classic crash when the adapter list is changed on a background thread or changed without notifying. Rule: mutate the backing list and call notify on the main thread, in the same message-queue turn, before the next layout pass.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
items.add(0, newItem); notifyItemInserted(0)
items.removeAt(i);     notifyItemRemoved(i)
notifyItemRangeChanged(start, count, PAYLOAD)

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Calling notifyItemRemoved(i) but forgetting notifyItemRangeChanged when you hold position-dependent UI (row numbers).
  • Updating the list from a worker thread: inconsistency crash.
  • Using notifyDataSetChanged "because it works" and losing scroll animation and, with images, doing 20 rebinds per refresh.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. When is notifyDataSetChanged acceptable? -> Whole dataset truly replaced, no animation wanted, small list.
  2. How do you stop it from resetting scroll? -> It doesn't reset scroll, but anchor positions can jump; DiffUtil retains anchor.
  3. Explain the "Inconsistency detected" crash. -> Adapter count changed without a matching notify before layout.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior explains invalidation flags, cache bypass, and prefers diffing over manual notify.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Pull-to-refresh using notifyDataSetChanged flashed all rows; DiffUtil made it a quiet in-place update.

questions.contextHtml:
A to-do screen with 400 rows. QA reports: "Tick row 2, scroll down, row 12 and 22 are also ticked. Sometimes tapping a row ticks a different row." Crash rate zero, no logs. Code:

class VH(val b: ItemTodoBinding) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(b.root)
override fun onBindViewHolder(h: VH, pos: Int) {
    val t = items[pos]
    h.b.title.text = t.title
    if (t.done) h.b.check.isChecked = true
    h.b.check.setOnCheckedChangeListener { _, checked -> items[pos].done = checked }
}

Rows are ~72dp, screen shows 9, device is a Pixel 6.
questions.promptHtml: Find the bugs and explain mechanically why they appear every ~10 rows.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Use notifyDataSetChanged" or "ListView has this issue", without seeing the missing else branch and the stale pos.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Is done stored in the model or only the view? Does the list change (insert/delete) while shown? Does the pattern appear after configuration change too?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Not an incident; a one-line fix is safe to hotfix.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) missing else isChecked = false; (b) listener installed before value set fires with stale pos; (c) pos captured goes stale after inserts/removals; (d) state restoration by id on config change (red herring since views have no ids).
  4. How I'd verify each: Toggle row 2, log h.bindingAdapterPosition and System.identityHashCode(h) in bind; the same holder id reappears at rows 12 and 22 (9 visible + 2 cache + prefetch gives ~10-row period).
  5. Root cause: Holder for row 2 is reused for row 12. Bind sets isChecked=true only for done rows, so false rows inherit true. Also the old listener from row 2 is still on that check box; setting isChecked can fire it and write to items[2].
  6. Fix:
override fun onBindViewHolder(h: VH, pos: Int) {
    val t = items[pos]
    h.b.title.text = t.title
    h.b.check.setOnCheckedChangeListener(null)
    h.b.check.isChecked = t.done
    h.b.check.setOnCheckedChangeListener { _, c ->
        val p = h.bindingAdapterPosition
        if (p != RecyclerView.NO_POSITION) onToggle(getItem(p).id, c)
    }
}

Better: set the listener once in onCreateViewHolder and read position at click time; push state to the ViewModel and let DiffUtil rebind. 7. Prevention: A bind unit/Espresso test with a list of 50 alternating states and scroll; code review rule "every branch sets every property"; lint-like checklist. 8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not setIsRecyclable(false) (disables reuse, hides bug, memory/jank); not notifyDataSetChanged on every toggle.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• What if I move the listener to onCreateViewHolder? -> Correct and cheaper; use bindingAdapterPosition and guard NO_POSITION.
  • Why does bindingAdapterPosition differ from layoutPosition? -> binding is adapter-data truth (updated after notify); layout position is what the last layout used (can lag one pass).
  • Does setHasStableIds fix it? -> No, model state is the fix.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A selection feature in a contacts list had "ghost selections" for months; the fix was a two-line bind change, but the real cost was five engineers each adding workarounds.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: blames notify or suggests disabling recycling.
  • Hire: finds missing else and stale pos, fixes in bind.
  • Strong hire: explains the ~10-row period, listener-fire-on-set, moves listener to create, uses model-driven state.

questions.promptHtml: What are change payloads in RecyclerView, how do you produce them with DiffUtil, and what goes wrong if you implement them incorrectly?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Tests depth beyond "use ListAdapter": partial binding, animation interaction, and correctness.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: A payload describes what changed in an item. DiffUtil.ItemCallback.getChangePayload(old, new) returns it, and RecyclerView calls onBindViewHolder(holder, position, payloads) with a non-empty list so I can update only the changed views. If I don't override the three-arg bind, it falls back to the full bind. A null payload means a full rebind.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Flow: areItemsTheSame true and areContentsTheSame false -> getChangePayload -> notifyItemRangeChanged(pos, 1, payload). Multiple changes to the same position before the next layout get merged: payloads accumulate in a list, so handle a list, not one object. Payloads also keep the same holder instance for change animations (DefaultItemAnimator cross-fades old/new holder only when there is no payload; with a payload, canReuseUpdatedViewHolder returns true and no cross-fade, which is why payload binds avoid flicker). Important: a payload bind must leave the row in the correct final state. If a holder was recycled and reused between the change and bind, a partial update leaves stale parts; that is why RecyclerView falls back to full bind if the holder is not in a bound state matching the old item.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
sealed interface Change { object Likes : Change; object Title : Change }
override fun getChangePayload(a: Post, b: Post): Any? = buildSet {
    if (a.likes != b.likes) add(Change.Likes)
    if (a.title != b.title) add(Change.Title)
}.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }

override fun onBindViewHolder(h: VH, pos: Int, payloads: MutableList<Any>) {
    if (payloads.isEmpty()) return super.onBindViewHolder(h, pos, payloads) // full bind
    val changes = payloads.flatMap { it as Set<*> }.toSet()
    val p = getItem(pos)
    if (Change.Likes in changes) h.b.likes.text = p.likes.toString()
    if (Change.Title in changes) h.b.title.text = p.title
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Forgetting payloads.isEmpty() full-bind branch: initial binds leave the row blank.
  • Assuming a single payload; they accumulate.
  • Payload includes mutable view references (leak).

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Does a payload bind skip the item animator? -> Cross-fade is skipped; the view is updated in place.
  2. When return null? -> When you want full rebind.
  3. Cost versus benefit? -> Helpful for heavy rows (images, rich text); for simple rows the diff itself costs more than the saved bind.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior knows payload accumulation, animator interaction and when partial bind is not worth it.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A live-score row updating every second flickered and rebuilt spans; payload for score only removed jank.

questions.promptHtml: What do setHasStableIds(true) and getItemId do, and do you need them with DiffUtil?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: People conflate DiffUtil identity with stable-id identity.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: Stable ids give each item a unique long id that survives position changes, so RecyclerView can match holders to items across notifyDataSetChanged, keep animations correct, and reuse scrap by id. With DiffUtil I usually don't need them because areItemsTheSame already provides identity, though they help with notifyDataSetChanged, selection libraries and state restoration.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: When enabled, the recycler tries to find a holder by id (getScrapOrHiddenOrCachedHolderForId) in addition to position. This makes notifyDataSetChanged cheaper: holders are not invalidated blindly and animations can run. Requirements: ids must be unique and stable; getItemId default returns NO_ID. Violations (duplicate ids) cause "Two different ViewHolders have the same stable ID" IllegalStateException. RecyclerView.Adapter throws if you call setHasStableIds after the adapter is attached with items. RecyclerView-Selection library requires stable ids. For ConcatAdapter see isolation modes (Q278). ListAdapter does not enable them by default.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
init { setHasStableIds(true) }
override fun getItemId(position: Int) = getItem(position).id   // Long, must be unique

For string ids use a hash with a collision-aware map, not hashCode() blindly.

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Using position as id, which defeats the point.
  • Using String.hashCode() of ids: collisions throw the duplicate crash.
  • Calling it required with DiffUtil: not required.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. What happens to a row if ids are stable and notifyDataSetChanged is called? -> Holder found by id, rebound, animation preserved.
  2. Does ListAdapter.submitList use getItemId? -> No, it uses areItemsTheSame.
  3. Why UUID strings are problematic? -> Need a long; map via an incrementing id table.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior separates DiffUtil identity from recycler id lookup and cites selection/state restoration use cases.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Selection tracker lost selection after refresh since item ids changed with list index.

questions.contextHtml: A news app (900k DAU) refreshes its feed every 30 seconds with silent polling. After a release, QA/users report the visible cards "blink" on every refresh and thumbnails reload (Glide network calls spiked 6x). Feed ~60 items. Code change in the release: adapter.items = newList; adapter.notifyDataSetChanged() replaced a ListAdapter. Server returns same data 95% of polls. Crash rate unchanged.
questions.promptHtml: Diagnose and fix it, and say how you'd prevent regressions.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Add a placeholder" or "cache images longer"; treats symptom, not the invalidate-all cause.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Did the change touch getItemId/stable ids? Are animations disabled? Is the blink on every poll or only on changed data? Same Glide cache settings?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Skip UI updates when newList == oldList (equality check) to stop 95% of blinks; ship hotfix.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) notifyDataSetChanged invalidates all holders so the animator cross-fades and Glide targets restart; (b) areContentsTheSame mismatch if I returned to ListAdapter (e.g. timestamp field changes each poll); (c) Glide thumbnails keyed by a URL with a rotating token (red herring unless URLs changed); (d) memory cache eviction.
  4. How I'd verify each: Layout Inspector bind counts / log in onBindViewHolder; Glide request logging (Glide.with log level); compare payload JSON for volatile fields; Network profiler for image fetches.
  5. Root cause: All holders flagged invalid; DefaultItemAnimator treats it as change -> cross-fade between old and new holder; bind restarts image loads; if URL signature includes a rotating token, memory-cache misses.
  6. Fix: Short-term equality skip. Long-term: restore ListAdapter with areItemsTheSame by id and areContentsTheSame over a UI model excluding volatile fields; call Glide.with(view).clear in onViewRecycled; use a stable key (signature) for images.
  7. Prevention: Unit test for the DiffUtil callback (same data -> no changes), Macrobenchmark scroll+refresh, lint/ review check banning notifyDataSetChanged.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not disabling item animations globally (hides issue); not raising cache sizes.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Only timestamp differs each poll; what do you do? -> Map to UI model without it, or make areContentsTheSame ignore it.
  • Server sends new item ordering each poll? -> areItemsTheSame by id still produces moves; consider detectMoves=false cost tradeoff.
  • Row jumps while user scrolls? -> Submit with commitCallback; preserve anchor.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A "perf cleanup" PR removed ListAdapter for simplicity; image CDN bill rose until someone saw the 6x image requests chart.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: image-cache tweaks only.
  • Hire: identifies notifyDataSetChanged, restores DiffUtil.
  • Strong hire: finds volatile fields, adds tests/monitoring, explains animator cross-fade and recycle clear.

questions.promptHtml: How does RecyclerView's ItemAnimator work, and how do you customise or disable it safely?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Animation bugs (flicker, blinking after update, weird move) are common and hinge on knowing the pre/post layout model.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: RecyclerView runs layout twice for animations: pre-layout records where views were, post-layout where they are, and the ItemAnimator animates the difference (add, remove, move, change). The default is DefaultItemAnimator; changes cross-fade from the old holder to a new one unless I return reuse from canReuseUpdatedViewHolder. To disable, set itemAnimator = null; to stop only change fades, set (itemAnimator as SimpleItemAnimator).supportsChangeAnimations = false.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Predictive animations: LayoutManager.supportsPredictiveItemAnimations() must be true; the RV does pre-layout (old positions plus disappearing items), then real layout. ItemHolderInfo captures bounds. Animators call dispatchAnimationFinished; item views with running animations have transient state and get onFailedToRecycleView. Payload binds avoid the change cross-fade by returning true from canReuseUpdatedViewHolder(holder, payloads) (DefaultItemAnimator does so when payloads non-empty). Custom animators extend SimpleItemAnimator or DefaultItemAnimator; durations: add/remove 120 ms, move/change 250 ms (default values in DefaultItemAnimator; verify).

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
(recycler.itemAnimator as? SimpleItemAnimator)?.supportsChangeAnimations = false
// or
recycler.itemAnimator = DefaultItemAnimator().apply { addDuration = 200; removeDuration = 150 }

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• itemAnimator = null to cure flicker (then removals pop).
  • Animating alpha/translation in bind and fighting the animator.
  • Stale transient state: views animating while recycled.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Why do inserts above the viewport shift items? -> Predictive layout and anchoring.
  2. Why a heavy bind makes animations stutter? -> Animations run on frame callbacks; bind blocks main thread.
  3. How to animate item expansion? -> TransitionManager/payload and layout change, or notifyItemChanged with payload and a custom animator.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior can explain pre-layout/post-layout and payload cross-fade interaction.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Chat bubbles flashed on each status update; supportsChangeAnimations=false plus payloads removed it.

questions.promptHtml: What is RecyclerView prefetch, how does GapWorker schedule it, and when does it fail to help?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Senior-level knowledge of how RecyclerView hides bind cost between frames.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: Since support lib 25.1, RecyclerView predicts which items the next frame needs along the scroll direction and binds them during idle time before the frame deadline, via GapWorker posting on frame callbacks. It prefetches up to the layout manager's prefetch count (for LinearLayoutManager the extra layout space; one extra item for grids typical) and puts holders into the cache/pool, so when scrolling reaches them, there is no create/bind. It helps when bind is short and the thread has slack; it cannot help if bind > idle time, or for fling that moves several items per frame.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: GapWorker is a Runnable that runs after the frame's draw using Choreographer frame time as a deadline estimate: it computes remaining time before the next vsync and skips tasks it can't finish (mDeadlineNs). Layout manager supplies tasks via collectAdjacentPrefetchPositions using LayoutPrefetchRegistry.addPosition(pos, distance); tasks sorted by distance (closest first). Prefetched holders land in the mCachedViews (if dispatchPrefetch) or pool; the pool entry is timed: RecycledViewPool records create/bind running averages (factorInCreateTime, willCreateInTime, willBindInTime) and does not prefetch if estimated cost exceeds the deadline. Nested lists: outer RV's GapWorker also prefetches inner RVs' first items, count set with LinearLayoutManager.setInitialPrefetchItemCount(n) (default 2; verify), useful only for horizontal lists inside vertical ones. Prefetch is on by default (setItemPrefetchEnabled(true) on layout manager). Disable only to isolate bugs.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
val lm = LinearLayoutManager(ctx, RecyclerView.HORIZONTAL, false)
lm.initialPrefetchItemCount = 4        // nested carousel inside vertical list
inner.layoutManager = lm
recycler.setItemViewCacheSize(4)       // optional: keep more already-bound off-screen views

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Setting initialPrefetchItemCount larger than visible items: wasted binds.
  • Believing prefetch removes the need for fast bind.
  • Using isNestedScrollingEnabled=false + wrapping heights, which breaks nested prefetch.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Why does a heavy bind still drop frames? -> Prefetch runs on main thread in idle slice; if one bind > slice, it is skipped or overruns.
  2. How verify prefetch works? -> Systrace/Perfetto slices "RV Prefetch" (verify slice name) and "RV OnBindView".
  3. Prefetch with a custom LayoutManager? -> Must implement collectAdjacentPrefetchPositions/collectInitialPrefetchPositions.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior knows it is deadline-based, per-type cost-estimated, and verifies in Perfetto.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A nested carousel stalled on first show until initialPrefetchItemCount matched the visible card count.

questions.contextHtml: A streaming-home screen: vertical RV of 25 rails, each a horizontal RV of up to 40 poster cards. After adding rails, p95 frame time on Redmi 9 (3 GB RAM) scroll went from 14 ms to 38 ms, jank 18%. Perfetto shows many Inflate slices (~6 ms each) in onCreateViewHolder for the inner cards during vertical scroll. Memory is also up 60 MB. Inner adapters are created per rail, each with its own default pool.
questions.promptHtml: Why is this slow and what do you change?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Use smaller images" or "reduce rails"; misses per-rail pools.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Are cards one view type? Is setHasFixedSize set? Are inner RVs created in the outer bind? Do inner RVs get detached state kept?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Limit to ~12 posters per rail initially; lower image resolution; ship config flag.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) every inner RV owns a pool so each new rail inflates its 5-6 cards again; (b) inner layout manager re-created in bind loses scroll and prefetch; (c) image decode on main; (d) no inner prefetch counts (red herring maybe).
  4. How I'd verify each: Perfetto count of Inflate per second; log RecycledViewPool.getRecycledViewCount; allocation profiler for holder instances; GPU rendering.
  5. Root cause: 25 rails x ~7 live holders = ~175 inflated cards; none shared. Each new rail scrolling in inflates; pool per RV only holds what it recycled.
  6. Fix:
class RailsAdapter(private val sharedPool: RecycledViewPool) : ... {
    override fun onCreateViewHolder(p: ViewGroup, t: Int) = RailVH(inflate(p)).also {
        it.rv.setRecycledViewPool(sharedPool)
        it.rv.layoutManager = LinearLayoutManager(p.context, HORIZONTAL, false)
            .apply { initialPrefetchItemCount = 4 }
        it.rv.setHasFixedSize(true)
    }
}
sharedPool.setMaxRecycledViews(CARD_TYPE, 20)   // 4 visible x ~5 rails offscreen

Create layout manager once in onCreateViewHolder, not bind. Save/restore inner scroll in onViewRecycled via layoutManager.onSaveInstanceState(). Keep the same card layout/holder class for the shared type. 7. Prevention: Macrobenchmark FrameTimingMetric on home; alert on janky-frame % in JankStats. 8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Pool max too large wastes memory (each holder ~ 20-40 KB with drawables; measure). Not nesting RV in ScrollView/NestedScrollView (measures all). Not disabling prefetch.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• What if cards differ by rail? -> One viewType per layout; the pool is keyed by viewType, so different layouts must have different type ints; only share same-holder types.
  • Compose migration? -> LazyColumn of LazyRow has no cross-row sharing; use contentType to enable composition reuse.
  • Memory regression? -> Trim pool in onTrimMemory via clear().

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A home screen jumped from 40% to 6% jank only by sharing one pool and moving LayoutManager creation out of bind; the "image optimisation" ticket was closed unused.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: image-size tweaks only.
  • Hire: shared pool + layout-manager-in-create.
  • Strong hire: sizes the pool, restores inner scroll, verifies with Perfetto, covers memory trim and Compose analog.

questions.promptHtml: What do setItemViewCacheSize, setMaxRecycledViews and setHasFixedSize(true) actually change, and when would you touch each?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Tuning knobs get cargo-culted; interviewers want mechanism and cost.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: setItemViewCacheSize(n) grows the position-matched cache (default 2) so recently scrolled-off rows return without rebinding, at the cost of keeping n attached-ready holders in memory. recycledViewPool.setMaxRecycledViews(type, n) raises the per-type pool cap (default 5) so create/inflate happens less. setHasFixedSize(true) promises the RecyclerView's own size does not depend on adapter content, so it skips a full requestLayout on item changes; it does not make items fixed.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Cache: wins when users scroll back and forth over the same few rows; useless for one-direction flings (use the pool/prefetch). Pool: wins when many holders are created, e.g. view-type heavy or nested lists. Memory math: if a holder costs ~30 KB (views + bitmaps references) and you raise cache from 2 to 10, that is ~240 KB extra; fine on a simple list, noticeable with big image rows on low-RAM devices. hasFixedSize: with match_parent size and no wrap_content, an adapter data change calls onItemRangeChanged handlers that avoid requestLayout() and only relayout children. If height is wrap_content, setting it true is a bug (the RV may not resize). Defaults: cache 2, pool 5 (from source constants; verify).

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
recycler.setHasFixedSize(true)               // RV bounds don't depend on adapter content
recycler.setItemViewCacheSize(6)
recycler.recycledViewPool.setMaxRecycledViews(TYPE_AD, 2)   // rarely seen type, keep small
recycler.recycledViewPool.setMaxRecycledViews(TYPE_ROW, 12)

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Setting cache size to 20+ as a magic fix: memory with no gain on one-direction scroll.
  • hasFixedSize(true) with wrap_content that must grow.
  • Expecting cache hits across different view types (cache is position-based; pool by type).

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Where do views go when cache is full? -> Oldest into the pool.
  2. How measure benefit? -> Count onBindViewHolder and onCreateViewHolder calls per scroll in a benchmark.
  3. Can pool be shared across Activities? -> Technically yes but holders hold Context; leak risk (see Q283).

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior quantifies memory and uses Perfetto bind/create counts to decide.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A team set cache size to 30 on a photo grid; OOM on 2 GB devices.

questions.promptHtml: What is the LayoutManager's job in RecyclerView, and what would you need to implement for a custom LayoutManager?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Tests whether you understand the division of labour and the cost of custom layout.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: RecyclerView measures itself; the LayoutManager owns child measurement, positioning, scrolling and what to recycle. A minimal custom LM implements generateDefaultLayoutParams, onLayoutChildren (fill views from the recycler), scrolling hooks (canScrollVertically/scrollVerticallyBy) that shift children and fill/recycle at edges, plus scroll-range methods and scrollToPosition/smoothScrollToPosition support.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Layout cycle: dispatchLayoutStep1 (pre-layout, record infos), Step2 (onLayoutChildren: detachAndScrapAttachedViews then loop recycler.getViewForPosition, addView, measureChildWithMargins, layoutDecorated), Step3 (animations). Scrolling: scrollBy(dy) -> shift children with offsetChildrenVertical, add views at the leading edge, removeAndRecycleView at the trailing edge, return consumed pixels. LinearLayoutManager does this with LayoutState and fill(). Other responsibilities: supportsPredictiveItemAnimations, onSaveInstanceState, accessibility, prefetch (collectAdjacentPrefetchPositions), computeVerticalScrollExtent/Offset/Range for scrollbars and fast scroll. Option ranking: ItemDecoration or SpanSizeLookup for grid variants -> StaggeredGridLayoutManager -> existing library (Flexbox, Google's FlexboxLayoutManager) -> custom LM. Custom LMs are the highest maintenance risk: state restore and animation bugs.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
class StackLM : RecyclerView.LayoutManager() {
    override fun generateDefaultLayoutParams() =
        RecyclerView.LayoutParams(WRAP_CONTENT, WRAP_CONTENT)
    override fun onLayoutChildren(r: RecyclerView.Recycler, s: RecyclerView.State) {
        detachAndScrapAttachedViews(r)
        var top = paddingTop
        for (i in 0 until itemCount) {
            val v = r.getViewForPosition(i); addView(v)
            measureChildWithMargins(v, 0, 0)
            val h = getDecoratedMeasuredHeight(v)
            layoutDecoratedWithMargins(v, paddingLeft, top, width - paddingRight, top + h)
            top += h
            if (top > height) break
        }
    }
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Laying out all items (O(N) layout) instead of stopping at viewport.
  • Forgetting detachAndScrapAttachedViews, creating duplicate children.
  • Ignoring State.isPreLayout leads to animation glitches.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Why does wrap_content on RV with a custom LM break? -> Needs isAutoMeasureEnabled() true.
  2. How do you support scrollbars? -> Implement the compute* methods.
  3. Why not do this in an ItemDecoration? -> Decorations only draw/offset; they can't position.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior lists cycle phases, recycling at edges, and argues for alternatives before building custom.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A carousel LM without prefetch hooks janked first scroll on low-end devices.

questions.contextHtml: Product wants a "circular wheel picker" of 3,000 items (cities) with snap-to-center and scaling of items near center, shipped in 3 weeks. Team has 2 Android devs, supports minSdk 24, 60 Hz and 120 Hz devices. A teammate proposes a custom LayoutManager ("full control"); another proposes ViewPager2; another suggests Compose LazyColumn with graphicsLayer.
questions.promptHtml: Which do you choose and how do you de-risk it?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: Picks custom LM for flexibility without cost/risk analysis.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Must it loop infinitely? Accessibility requirements? Is the rest of the screen Compose? Is item content simple text?
  2. Immediate mitigation: N/A; define a spike: 2 days to prototype the least risky option.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) LinearLayoutManager + LinearSnapHelper + scale in onScrolled (cheap, 90% of the look); (b) LazyColumn with snapFlingBehavior and graphicsLayer scaling by layoutInfo; (c) custom LM only if circular geometry (curved positioning) is mandatory.
  4. How I'd verify each: Prototype spike measured by Macrobenchmark frame timing on a mid device at 120 Hz; TalkBack walk-through.
  5. Root cause: The "need" is visual scaling and snapping, not a new layout algorithm; those are decorations over linear layout.
  6. Fix (decision): LinearLayoutManager + LinearSnapHelper; scale each child using distance to center in onScrolled; infinite looping by adapter getItemCount = Int.MAX_VALUE with position % size (note: breaks DiffUtil; keep size small). Custom LM later if curved offset needed; implement with LinearLayoutManager subclass overriding scrollVerticallyBy to post-process children (less code than full LM).
LinearSnapHelper().attachToRecyclerView(rv)
rv.addOnScrollListener(object : RecyclerView.OnScrollListener() {
    override fun onScrolled(r: RecyclerView, dx: Int, dy: Int) {
        val mid = r.height / 2f
        for (i in 0 until r.childCount) {
            val c = r.getChildAt(i)
            val d = abs(mid - (c.top + c.height / 2f)) / mid
            c.scaleX = 1f - 0.3f * d; c.scaleY = c.scaleX
        }
    }
})
  1. Prevention: Keep a visual regression screenshot test and a benchmark; document the design.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not custom LM in a 3-week window with 2 devs (state restore, a11y, animations multiply scope). Not ViewPager2 (paging semantic, wrong for 3,000-item picker).

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Needs curved arc positions? -> Subclass LinearLayoutManager and apply translation post-layout; or custom LM with prefetch.
  • Items mutate while scrolling? -> DiffUtil with the finite list; loop via a repeating index, not Int.MAX.
  • Compose app? -> LazyColumn is fine; interop via ComposeView if only a part is Compose.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A custom carousel LM took three sprints and still failed a11y; the replacement was snap helper + scale callback in 120 lines.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: chooses custom LM by default.
  • Hire: picks snap helper + scale with reason.
  • Strong hire: scopes spike, compares Compose, lists custom-LM costs, offers the subclass escape hatch.

questions.promptHtml: How does ConcatAdapter work, how does it handle view types and stable ids, and when would you use it versus one adapter with multiple types?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Checks modern composition patterns and edge-case knowledge (pool sharing, ids).

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: ConcatAdapter (RecyclerView 1.2.0+) presents several adapters in sequence in one RecyclerView, e.g. header, content, load-state footer. By default each child adapter's view types are isolated (remapped), so each has its own pool entries. I use it to compose independent adapters (header + paged list + footer); I use one adapter with multiple view types when rows come from one heterogeneous list with shared diffing.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: ConcatAdapter.Config(isolateViewTypes, stableIdMode): with isolateViewTypes=true (default) child adapters can use the same int types without clashes and don't share holders; set false to share holders of the same type among adapters (then types must truly be the same layout/holder). StableIdMode: NO_STABLE_IDS (default), ISOLATED_STABLE_IDS (each adapter's ids remapped to avoid collisions; children must have stable ids), SHARED_STABLE_IDS (ids already unique across adapters). Child adapters can be added/removed dynamically (addAdapter, removeAdapter) and each manages its own notify calls; ConcatAdapter offsets positions. Paging 3 uses it via withLoadStateFooter. Multi-type in one adapter: getItemViewType returns a type; sealed UI model, ListAdapter<UiItem, RecyclerView.ViewHolder>; one DiffUtil over the sealed hierarchy.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
val config = ConcatAdapter.Config.Builder().setIsolateViewTypes(true)
    .setStableIdMode(ConcatAdapter.Config.StableIdMode.NO_STABLE_IDS).build()
recycler.adapter = ConcatAdapter(config, headerAdapter, contentAdapter, footerAdapter)

override fun getItemViewType(pos: Int) = when (getItem(pos)) {
    is UiItem.Header -> R.layout.item_header      // layout id as type
    is UiItem.Post -> R.layout.item_post
}

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Calling setHasStableIds(true) on children without matching Config mode: crash or mismatched ids.
  • Header adapter that changes item count via notifyDataSetChanged every time.
  • One giant when binder with nullable fields instead of a sealed type.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Click position in a child adapter? -> bindingAdapterPosition is relative to the child adapter; absoluteAdapterPosition is relative to the concat.
  2. Share holder between adapters? -> isolateViewTypes=false with identical types.
  3. Header scrolling/sticky? -> Sticky needs ItemDecoration or custom handling.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior knows isolation modes, position APIs and stable-id config.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: A banner adapter using type 0 collided with the list's type 0 in a custom concat before ConcatAdapter existed.

questions.promptHtml: What are the correct and incorrect ways to handle clicks in RecyclerView items, and what are the position-related bugs?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Checks understanding of holder positions during animations and updates.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: Set the click listener once in onCreateViewHolder (not every bind), and at click time read bindingAdapterPosition (not the position arg captured in bind); guard for RecyclerView.NO_POSITION since the holder can be removed while a click is in flight. Use the item id from the model rather than the position when calling business logic.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Position flavors: getAdapterPosition() (deprecated in 1.2.0 for bindingAdapterPosition/absoluteAdapterPosition), getLayoutPosition() (position as of last layout pass). During notify with pending layout, adapter position is the updated truth while layout position lags; NO_POSITION (-1) appears when the holder was removed or the adapter has pending updates that haven't dispatched. Setting listeners in bind allocates a lambda per bind (GC churn) and captures stale positions after insertions (bind is not re-run for items shifted by an insert above). Also: setOnClickListener on the root only covers unconsumed taps; child buttons need their own listener; android:clickable/focusable on root for ripple/accessibility; double-tap guard for navigation; ListAdapter.getItem(position).

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
class VH(val b: ItemBinding, onClick: (Long) -> Unit) : RecyclerView.ViewHolder(b.root) {
    init {
        b.root.setOnClickListener {
            val p = bindingAdapterPosition
            if (p != RecyclerView.NO_POSITION) onClick(currentItemId(p))
        }
    }
}

(Where currentItemId reads from the adapter, e.g. an inner class or lambda getItem(p).id.)

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Capturing pos in bind: after an insert at 0 the closure points at the wrong item.
  • Not guarding NO_POSITION: IndexOutOfBounds when tapping a row that is animating out.
  • Storing a reference to the Activity in the holder.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Difference between adapter and layout position? -> Adapter = data truth, layout = last laid out.
  2. Concat/nested position? -> bindingAdapterPosition relative to bound adapter.
  3. Use OnItemTouchListener? -> Only for gesture-level logic; it bypasses child click semantics.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior states why bind-time listeners go stale, uses ids instead of positions, handles NO_POSITION and a11y.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: "Delete" removed the wrong email after a new message arrived at the top; closure held an old position.

questions.contextHtml: A marketplace listing screen (1.2M DAU) with ~5,000 loaded results. After a redesign, p95 frame time while scrolling is 29 ms on mid-range devices (Pixel 4a-class, 60 Hz), janky-frame rate 22% (was 4%). Perfetto: onBindViewHolder takes 9-14 ms per row; inside it, SimpleDateFormat creation, Html.fromHtml for descriptions, and a 4-level nested LinearLayout per row. Images load via Glide. Logcat shows Skipped 31 frames.
questions.promptHtml: How do you triage and cut jank, in what order?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Move to Compose" or "run bind in a coroutine", which breaks bind semantics.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Jank on first scroll only, or sustained? Which device tier? Did layout change or data? Is it measure/layout (Choreographer#doFrame breakdown) or bind?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Cache the SimpleDateFormat/formatted strings; trim description to plain text; ship; roll back image size changes if any.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) heavy bind work on main thread; (b) deep view hierarchy => measure/layout cost (4 nested LinearLayouts with weights double-measure); (c) onCreateViewHolder inflation on fling (pool too small); (d) Glide decoding sizes too big (red herring if flame chart shows no decode on main).
  4. How I'd verify each: Perfetto/System Trace slices (RV OnBindView, RV CreateView, Inflate, measure/layout); Layout Inspector depth; JankStats per-state; Macrobenchmark FrameTimingMetric.
  5. Root cause: Bind does ~10 ms of CPU; at 60 Hz the 16.6 ms budget leaves ~6 ms for measure/layout/draw/RenderThread, so a frame that binds 2 rows blows it. Prefetch cannot hide a bind longer than idle slice.
  6. Fix: Precompute display strings off main in the mapper to a UI model (formatted date, parsed spans) and bind just sets text; hoist formatters to a singleton; flatten to ConstraintLayout (aim for depth <= 3); setHasFixedSize(true); pool/cache sizing; Glide override(w,h) thumbnails; payload for partial updates. Result target: bind < 2 ms, jank <= 5%.
  7. Prevention: Macrobenchmark in CI with threshold; JankStats in prod; lint on SimpleDateFormat in bind; PR checklist.
  8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not async bind (race with recycle); not setItemViewCacheSize(50); not giving up animations globally.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Jank only on 120 Hz devices? -> Budget 8.3 ms; same fix, stricter thresholds.
  • Rich text needed? -> Precompute Spannable off main; use PrecomputedText (AppCompatTextView setTextFuture).
  • First frame after navigation janks? -> Inflation of the whole list; pre-warm pool in a background-inflation (AsyncLayoutInflater is deprecated in some versions; verify) or lighter item layout.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A single Html.fromHtml at ~6 ms in bind was the whole regression; moving it to the mapper dropped jank from 22% to 5% in a one-file PR.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: random optimisations without measurement.
  • Hire: traces bind and layout, moves work out of bind.
  • Strong hire: budget math per refresh rate, flattens hierarchy, adds CI benchmark/JankStats guardrails.

questions.contextHtml:
A chat list uses ListAdapter<Message, VH>. Bug reports: "New messages sometimes don't appear until another message arrives" and, separately, ANR traces showing DiffUtil.calculateDiff on the main thread for 1.4 s (list of 30k messages after history import). Code:

val list = adapter.currentList as MutableList<Message>
list.add(newMessage)
adapter.submitList(list)

// elsewhere, import path
val diff = DiffUtil.calculateDiff(MsgCallback(old, new), true)
diff.dispatchUpdatesTo(adapter)
questions.promptHtml: What are the bugs and how do you fix each?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Call notifyDataSetChanged after submitList".

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Is currentList mutable (it's unmodifiable in ListAdapter; cast may throw UnsupportedOperationException)? Who owns the source list? How big is import?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Always submit a new copy: submitList(list + newMessage); for the import, route through submitList not manual calculateDiff on main.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) same-instance submit is ignored (newList === mList), or cast mutation breaks diff snapshot; (b) calculateDiff is synchronous, O(N + D^2) with moves detection, 30k items on main; (c) detectMoves=true adds sort cost; (d) race with background mutation.
  4. How I'd verify each: Log currentList === newList; ANR trace/StrictMode; Perfetto slice for DiffUtil.
  5. Root cause: Mutating the list AsyncListDiffer already holds makes old==new, so the diff finds nothing; the next message appears only when a new list instance gets submitted. Manual calculateDiff blocks main.
  6. Fix:
adapter.submitList(adapter.currentList + newMessage) { list.scrollToPosition(adapter.itemCount - 1) }
// import: keep source in ViewModel as immutable List, emit via StateFlow; collect and submitList
// or for huge lists, compute diff on Dispatchers.Default yourself and dispatch on main, or paginate

For 30k, use paging (Paging 3 PagingDataAdapter) so lists stay ~50-200 items in memory windows. 7. Prevention: Immutable List in state (Kotlin List, data classes); unit test for the diff callback; StrictMode/ANR monitoring. 8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not detectMoves=false blindly (breaks move animation); not runBlocking on main.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Two quick submits? -> Latest wins; earlier diff results dropped via generation counter.
  • Need diff result sync in tests? -> Provide executors via AsyncDifferConfig.
  • Scroll to bottom on new message but not when user scrolled up? -> Check findLastVisibleItemPosition before submit.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: Customer-support app froze for 2 s when opening large threads; replacing main-thread calculateDiff and chunking history fixed the ANR cluster.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: notifyDataSetChanged workaround.
  • Hire: new list instance; async diff.
  • Strong hire: explains generation/latest-wins, complexity, paging, scroll policy.

questions.promptHtml: After rotation, the RecyclerView scroll position is lost when data loads asynchronously. Why, and how does StateRestorationPolicy fix it?

sections.label: Why interviewers ask this
sections.html: Real apps load data async; interviewers want to know you understand the layout-time restore model.

sections.label: 30-second answer
sections.html: RecyclerView restores the LayoutManager state (anchor position and offset) when it first lays out, but if the adapter is empty then, the restore is dropped or clamped. Adapter.stateRestorationPolicy = PREVENT_WHEN_EMPTY (RecyclerView 1.2.0+) delays restoration until the adapter has items; PREVENT delays until I set it to ALLOW. Paging adapters use it.

sections.label: Deep explanation
sections.html: Restore flow: onRestoreInstanceState stores pending saved state; dispatchLayoutStep calls LayoutManager.onRestoreInstanceState when mAdapter.canRestoreState() is true. The policy controls that predicate. Values: ALLOW (default), PREVENT_WHEN_EMPTY, PREVENT. Requirements: RV must have an id (or view-saved-state key), the LayoutManager must be set before restore and must support restore (LinearLayoutManager does); ViewModel retains data, so data arrives from memory immediately in most cases; with disk/network load it arrives after first layout. Alternatives: keep the LM state manually in the ViewModel (layoutManager.onSaveInstanceState()), restore after first submitList commit callback.

sections.label: Code
sections.html:
adapter.stateRestorationPolicy = RecyclerView.Adapter.StateRestorationPolicy.PREVENT_WHEN_EMPTY
recycler.adapter = adapter
viewModel.items.collect { adapter.submitList(it) }   // restore happens when list becomes non-empty

For header + content in ConcatAdapter, ConcatAdapter aggregates policy; a header-only adapter makes it non-empty, so use PREVENT on the concat until content loaded (verify behavior per version).

sections.label: Common mistakes & traps
sections.html:
• Recreating the adapter/LM on every onViewCreated in fragments: state lost on back navigation (view destroyed). Hold adapter reference per view lifecycle, null it in onDestroyView.
  • Setting scrollToPosition(saved) too early.
  • No ids, saveEnabled=false.

sections.label: Follow-ups
sections.html:
1. Fragment back stack case? -> View recreated; LM state restored from the saved view state if submitList data present; policy still needed.
  2. Nested RV state? -> Must save/restore per inner LM (Q274).
  3. Paging 3? -> Adapter sets the policy itself.

sections.label: 3-YOE vs senior answer
sections.html: Senior explains restore timing, header-only pitfall, fragment back stack behavior.

sections.label: Production connection
sections.html: Product detail "back" always returned to top until PREVENT_WHEN_EMPTY was set.

questions.subtopic: Leaks via holders and shared pools
questions.contextHtml: Post-incident review: OOM crash rate went from 0.15% to 0.9% on 2-3 GB devices after "share one RecycledViewPool across all list screens" shipped. Heap dumps show 14 destroyed ProductActivity instances retained; GC root is a static RecycledViewPool held in a singleton ListPools object; holders reference itemView.context. Fragment ViewBinding references in holders also seen. LeakCanary in debug wasn't run on those flows.
questions.promptHtml: Explain the root cause, the fix and what process would have caught it.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Use WeakReference everywhere", treats symptom.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Are pool consumers on different themes/contexts? Are holders created with Activity context? Did the pool previously live per RV?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Disable shared singleton via remote flag; roll back release if flag unavailable.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) pool in a static object holds ViewHolder -> itemView -> Context (Activity); (b) holders also hold fragment binding; (c) image loaders registered per holder not cleared; (d) a bitmap cache (red herring).
  4. How I'd verify each: Heap dump in Android Studio / LeakCanary: shortest path to GC root; count ViewHolder per type; memory profiler allocations.
  5. Root cause: RecycledViewPool holds recycled ViewHolders strongly; each holder's views reference the Activity context used to inflate them. Static pool outlives Activities, so every Activity visited stays alive. (Also a theme bug: holders inflated in Activity A's theme reused in B.)
  6. Fix: Scope the pool to the host: pool in the Activity/ViewModel-tied owner, recyclerView.setRecycledViewPool(pool) for lists on the same screen only; call pool.clear() in onDestroyView/onDestroy; never keep a pool in a singleton; use ContextThemeWrapper consistency; null binding in onDestroyView; onViewRecycled clears image requests.
class HomeFragment : Fragment() {
    private val pool = RecyclerView.RecycledViewPool()
    override fun onDestroyView() { pool.clear(); recycler.adapter = null; super.onDestroyView() }
}
  1. Prevention: LeakCanary in debug/internal builds, instrumentation tests that open/close screens 20x and assert no leak; code review rule on statics holding views; StrictMode.detectActivityLeaks (verify).
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not keeping a static pool "for perf"; benefit is minor vs leak risk. Not WeakReference<Pool>.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Share across tabs in same Activity? -> Fine; owner is the Activity.
  • Application context for inflation? -> Wrong theme/styles (Application context ignores theme/dark mode attributes).
  • Pool max size vs memory? -> Cap with setMaxRecycledViews.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A "perf win" on a benchmark (cold inflate savings) shipped with a static pool; it only appeared in production after users navigated 10+ screens.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: adds weak refs.
  • Hire: scopes pool and clears on destroy.
  • Strong hire: explains holder->context chain, theme mismatch, heap dump process, CI leak tests.

questions.contextHtml: A messaging app's chat RV (reversed stackFromEnd=true, ~20k DAU growing to 200k) loads older messages when the user scrolls to top (pagination 50 per page) and receives live messages at the bottom. Reports: on loading older pages the list "jumps" to the top ~15% of the time; live messages auto-scroll even when the user is reading history; at 10x load, bursts of 30 messages/s from group chats cause 40 ms frames and submitList storms (each triggers a diff of 2,000 items).
questions.promptHtml: How do you make scroll anchoring stable and the update path scale?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: scrollToPosition after each update.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Reverse layout or stackFromEnd? Ids stable? Is the list ordered newest-last with DB (Room) as source? Is update delivered as full list each time?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Debounce/batch live messages to 100-250 ms; only auto-scroll if user was at bottom.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) prepend with notifyDataSetChanged or wrong diff identity loses anchor; (b) submitList race with scrollToPosition before commit; (c) full-list diff per message (2,000 items x 30/s); (d) image heights unknown, causing re-layout (red herring partially).
  4. How I'd verify each: Log anchor item id before/after commit; Perfetto for diff and layout slices; record message-burst replay.
  5. Root cause: LinearLayoutManager keeps its anchor by position; when items are inserted above without proper notify, anchor shifts; DiffUtil inserts are dispatched as notifyItemRangeInserted which LM compensates for only if areItemsTheSame by id is correct and commitCallback timing is respected.
  6. Fix: Stable ids/areItemsTheSame by message id; layoutManager.stackFromEnd = true for chat or reverse layout (reverseLayout=true with newest at index 0 keeps prepend anchored without adjusting); decide autoscroll in the commit callback using pre-submit "isAtBottom"; coalesce updates with conflate + debounce; compute diff off main (ListAdapter does); keep an in-memory window via Paging 3 with Room RemoteMediator for history.
val atBottom = !recycler.canScrollVertically(1)
adapter.submitList(newList) { if (atBottom) recycler.scrollToPosition(adapter.itemCount - 1) }
  1. Prevention: Instrumented test simulating prepend + live burst; benchmark; metrics on diff time via Trace.beginSection.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not restoring by pixel offset manually (fragile with variable heights); not disabling animations as a fix.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Messages edited in place? -> payloads, same id.
  • User scrolled up and new messages arrive? -> Show "N new" chip rather than scroll.
  • Variable-height images shifting layout? -> Reserve aspect-ratio space from metadata.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: Group-chat bursts caused diff storms; adding 150 ms batching cut main-thread time by ~70% with no visible delay.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: scrollToPosition hacks.
  • Hire: id-based diff, at-bottom check in commit callback, batching.
  • Strong hire: reverse layout reasoning, paging with DB, measured diff cost, UX for unread chip.
